ai.summary: The Freebuff CLI now detects and resumes legacy single-session hours left behind by pre-multi-session binaries during cross-protocol update restarts. ai.title: Binary elision and end-based rewind counts added to compaction
ai.summary: Model-based context compaction now elides large base64 payloads from tool results during summarization, preventing binary data from inflating token counts and forcing multiple sequential LLM calls. The SDK's `truncateRunStateAtUserTurn` function was updated to count only messages tagged `USER_PROMPT` and to accept an optional `totalUserTurns` parameter that places the cut from the end of the history, ensuring edits to recent messages in compacted threads preserve earlier context. This fixes a bug where system-generated notes and compacted summaries were incorrectly counted as user turns, causing the rewind to move earlier than intended.
ai.evidence: In `packages/agent-runtime/src/model-compaction.ts`, the `elideBinaryStrings` replacer and `omittedBinary` helper are introduced to replace raw `JSON.stringify(part)` calls during history serialization. In `sdk/src/compact-run-state.ts`, `truncateRunStateAtUserTurn` now filters for `USER_PROMPT` tags and supports a new `totalUserTurns` parameter for end-based counting.
ai.unknowns: The diff does not show the specific host application that currently passes the `totalUserTurns` parameter to `truncateRunStateAtUserTurn`.

changes.what: Added binary string elision to model compaction serialization to exclude large base64 payloads from summarizer requests.
Updated `truncateRunStateAtUserTurn` to filter for `USER_PROMPT` tags and support end-based counting via `totalUserTurns`.

eli5.text: When the assistant summarizes a long conversation to fit more into its memory, it now skips over large chunks of image data instead of copying them, which prevents these summary tasks from taking several minutes and blocking your chat. If you edit a message in a long thread, the assistant now remembers only the exact conversation up to that point, instead of accidentally forgetting earlier parts of the discussion because it miscounted internal notes as your messages. These fixes make the assistant faster and more reliable when handling long sessions with images.

ai.title: Release 0.0.203 adds binary elision and end-based rewind counts
ai.summary: Release 0.0.203 of the Freebuff CLI bundles updates to the agent runtime's compaction logic and the SDK's run-state rewind mechanics. In `packages/agent-runtime/src/model-compaction.ts`, a `JSON.stringify` replacer now substitutes base64 and data-URL media payloads with named omissions instead of serializing their bytes, preventing massive token counts during model summarization. In `sdk/src/compact-run-state.ts`, `truncateRunStateAtUserTurn` now accepts an optional `totalUserTurns` parameter to calculate the rewind boundary by counting `USER_PROMPT` tags backward from the end of the message history.
ai.evidence: The release diff in `freebuff/cli/release/package.json` bumps the version field from `0.0.202` to `0.0.203`. The included release member evidence for commit `24636b01` shows new functions `omittedBinary` and `elideBinaryStrings` added to `packages/agent-runtime/src/model-compaction.ts`, and a new `totalUserTurns` parameter added to `truncateRunStateAtUserTurn` in `sdk/src/compact-run-state.ts`.
ai.unknowns: The omitted first change in the release window is not visible in the provided evidence.

eli5.text: This release improves how the assistant manages long coding conversations and undoes your edits. When the chat gets very long, the assistant now creates a written summary to fit into its memory; if that summary would include large image files or base64 data, it replaces those blocks with a short note instead of copying them, preventing the summary process from hanging or crashing. When you undo a specific message in a long chat, the assistant now correctly identifies which of your original prompts to keep versus delete. Previously, it counted notes the system adds (like cancellation messages) as if they were your prompts, which caused it to accidentally delete more of your conversation than you intended when you used undo. This means your chat history now stays aligned with your visible transcript after you edit or cancel parts of it.

entries.title: CLI update: chat
entries.summary: New files: `cli/src/utils/fatal-crash-report.ts`.

ai.title: Add crash telemetry, SIGPIPE guard, and session resume on external
ai.summary: The CLI now writes a bounded fatal crash report synchronously on uncaught exceptions, which the next launch ships as `CLI_FATAL_CRASH`, and treats external termination signals like SIGHUP or SIGTERM as reasons to keep an active Freebuff session for resumption rather than releasing it. `SIGPIPE` is now ignored and excluded from the renderer's exit signals to prevent broken pipes from tearing down the UI or killing the process. Additionally, inline response ads use a stable `NO_RESPONSE_ADS` constant instead of a fresh object when hidden to prevent excessive re-renders, and SDK event handlers are wrapped to isolate UI state update failures from the agent run.
ai.evidence: New file cli/src/utils/fatal-crash-report.ts defines recordFatalCrashSync and takePreviousFatalCrash; cli/src/index.tsx imports takePreviousFatalCrash to ship AnalyticsEvent.CLI_FATAL_CRASH at startup; cli/src/utils/renderer-cleanup.ts adds CLI_RENDERER_EXIT_SIGNALS, ignores SIGPIPE, and calls handleExternalExit for SIGHUP/SIGTERM; cli/src/state/freebuff-session-store.ts adds keepSlotForResume to preserve active Freebuff sessions on external exit.

changes.what: Introduces `fatal-crash-report.ts` to write and ship bounded crash telemetry as `CLI_FATAL_CRASH` on the next launch.
Adds `keepSlotForResume` to preserve active Freebuff sessions when the CLI exits via external signals like SIGHUP or SIGTERM.
Excludes `SIGPIPE` from renderer exit signals and ignores it in process handlers to prevent broken pipes from destroying the UI.
Wraps SDK stream and event handlers in `isolateUiHandler` to catch UI state update errors and log them without terminating the agent run.
Uses a stable frozen `NO_RESPONSE_ADS` object and `visibleResponseAds` helper to avoid identity changes when inline ads are hidden.

eli5.text: The command-line assistant now saves a short note if it crashes, which it automatically sends on your next start so the makers can fix the problem. It also prevents the program from quitting when a terminal connection drops or when you close the window, letting you resume your active free coding session instead of losing it. These changes keep the interface stable and help developers who use the free tier recover from unexpected interruptions.

ai.title: Freebuff CLI 0.0.204 release with crash telemetry and session resume
ai.summary: Release 0.0.204 packages the new fatal crash reporting mechanism where the CLI writes a bounded crash report locally and ships it on the next launch. External exit signals like SIGHUP or SIGTERM now keep an active Freebuff session slot so the next launch can resume the purchased hour instead of releasing it. The release also refactors the CLI claim prefix to use a shared constant and adds a helper function to identify CLI claims.
ai.evidence: The diff shows `freebuff/cli/release/package.json` bumping the version from 0.0.203 to 0.0.204. The member diff in `cli/src/utils/fatal-crash-report.ts` introduces `takePreviousFatalCrash` and `recordFatalCrashSync` to ship previous-launch fatal crash telemetry on the next startup, while `cli/src/utils/renderer-cleanup.ts` adds `CLI_RENDERER_EXIT_SIGNALS` to ignore SIGPIPE and `handleExternalExit` to preserve active Freebuff sessions on external signals.

changes.what: Introduced a fatal crash report module that writes a bounded JSON file on fatal exit and ships it as a telemetry event on the next launch.
Added logic to keep active Freebuff session slots on external exit signals to allow resumption on the next launch, and prevented SIGPIPE from terminating the process.
Defined `FREEBUFF_CLI_CLAIM_PREFIX` and `isFreebuffCliClaim` in the shared desktop sessions constants to identify CLI claims on the purchase protocol.
Updated the CLI session identity module to use the shared `FREEBUFF_CLI_CLAIM_PREFIX` constant instead of a local string literal.
Wrapped SDK event handlers in an isolation layer to prevent React state update errors from crashing the agent run and introduced a static frozen object for empty ad responses.
Bumped the Freebuff CLI release version to 0.0.204.

eli5.text: Freebuff CLI 0.0.204 adds automatic crash reporting so that if the app unexpectedly stops, the next time you open it sends a short summary of what went wrong to the developers. It also prevents you from losing a paid session if you close the terminal window or force-quit the app; your active time is now preserved so you can pick up where you left off when you reopen it. A fix ensures that when ads are hidden, the chat interface does not freeze or crash during fast streaming. Additionally, the app now handles several system exit signals more gracefully, ensuring it cleans up properly instead of leaving a frozen screen or a hidden background process. If the interface glitches while the AI is working, the session will continue running in the background rather than terminating immediately.

ai.title: Freebuff CLI moves model selection to /model and adds send-time
ai.summary: This commit removes the `/reasoning` slash command and introduces `/model` to open the in-chat model picker, replacing the previous landing-screen-only selection flow. The new `FreebuffChatControls` and `useFreebuffChatAdmission` hook defer session admission to the moment a user sends their first message, allowing model switches and wallet consent without terminating the active session. Several supporting changes include a new `FreebuffChatFooter` displaying the current model, a rewritten `HelpBanner` with keyboard shortcut groups, and `AI_SDK_LOG_WARNINGS` redirection to keep SDK diagnostics off the terminal.

Adds new Freebuff-specific chat UI components including a header with session metadata, a footer with model status, and updated status bar styling for the Freebuff variant.
Rewrites the HelpBanner to display grouped keyboard shortcuts and adds `?` and `←` keybindings for empty input to trigger help and history.
Redirects AI SDK warnings to the internal logger to prevent them from overwriting the terminal UI and extracts the Freebuff wordmark into a dedicated utility.

eli5.text: Choosing which AI model to use now happens while you are chatting, not just when you first open the app. The old command for adjusting how hard the model thinks has been removed; that setting now lives inside the new model-choice screen, so you pick the model and its thinking depth in one place. This affects you every time you use the free coding assistant in your terminal: if you cancel a model switch or change your mind before sending a message, your chat stays exactly where it was, and a new line at the bottom of the screen shows which model is currently active and how to change it.
